Ever since the inception of them, the nature of the internet changed dramatically. I feel like we've not yet fully understood the repercussions of them altogether.

Before social media, it was flat out stupid to put your name out there on the internet. Maybe I'm just older, and my parent's were strict, but pre-Myspace days it was well-known you'd have to be batshit stupid to even think about putting your full name and address out there for anyone to view. These days, people are used to putting recent pictures up, their birthdate, their full name, their address, and everything else going on in their lives just right to their Facebook account.

Because people are used to being that free with their personal information, other sites realized they can track quite a bit more data from their potential customers. There's more tracking going on. Between google and face book's databases, you're guaranteed to get swamped by targeted ads no matter where you go on the internet. Before the days of myspace, it would've been unheard of to post personal information unless you were buying something to be shipped to your home.

In case you were wondering, this is why the internet has been around for decades but Doxxing is a more recent phenomenon of the last 5-10 years. Because before Myspace, no one would have put the information out there for the taking. Now, everyone puts all of their information out there and makes it fucking easy to figure out who you are, where you work, what you look like, who your loved ones are, and where you live. Fuck, it's not even hard to figure out how many people are going to be in that home most of the time. If you're really clever, you can monitor Facebook activity to plan out a robbery or worse without even being friends with anyone in the household.

There is a need for anonymity on the internet, and it's being quickly forgotten, and the consequences certainly aren't being told like they should be. Myspace died when it hit the news how easily pedophiles were using it to get victims, but all that did was kill that social media platform, but not the idea of a social media platform itself. Everyone just transferred over to Facebook instead and began doing the exact same behavior, or began putting even more out there.

The problem is that when the information is open and available, people will look at it. In our stupidity, we only get upset when no one is looking.
